auc_target.label: Daily AUC target for serious MRSA infection (adults and paediatrics)
auc_target.quote: Daily AUC values (assuming a MICBMD of 1 mg/L) should be main- tained between 400 and 600 mg·h/L to maximize efficacy and minimize the likelihood of AKI.

neonatal.label: Neonates and infants up to 3 months: dose range to reach AUC 400 mg·h/L
neonatal.quote: Doses recommended to achieve an AUC of 400 mg·h/L (assuming a MIC of 1 mg/L) in neonates and infants up to 3 months old range from 10 to 20 mg/kg every 8 to 48 hours, depending on postmenstrual age, weight, and SCr (A-II).

neonatal.label: Trough 7 to 11 mg/L predicted AUC24 above 400 in at least 90% of neonates (Frymoyer model)
neonatal.quote: trough concentra- tions ranging from 7 to 11 mg/L were highly predictive of an AUC 24 of >400 mg·h/L in at least 90% of neonates.

neonatal.label: Trough 11 mg/L predicted AUC of 400 or more in 93% of neonates, but trough alone is imprecise
neonatal.quote: While a trough concentration of 11 mg/L predicted the attainment of an AUC of ≥400 mg·h/L in 93% of neonates, Stockmann and colleagues noted that a trough concen- tration alone did not precisely predict AUC and concluded that Bayesian ap- proaches to support vancomycin dosing decisions for neonates in the clinical setting are needed.

neonatal.label: No consensus neonatal dosing model
neonatal.quote: However, when evaluating published neonatal PK models, no consensus on an optimal dosing regimen was achieved by experts on neonatal vancomycin, Zhao et al reported.

trough_only.label: Trough-only monitoring at 15 to 20 mg/L is no longer recommended (serious MRSA)
trough_only.quote: Trough-only monitoring, with a target of 15 to 20 mg/L, is no longer recommended based on efficacy and nephrotoxicity data in patients with serious infections due to MRSA (A-II).

sampling.label: Two-level sampling for equation-based AUC: post-distributional peak and trough in the same interval
sampling.quote: It is preferred that a near steady-state, postdistributional peak (1 to 2 hours after end of infusion) and trough con- centrations within the same dosing interval (if possible) are used when estimating the AUC with the equation- based methods.

sampling.label: Scale the one-interval AUC to 24 h by the number of doses per day
sampling.quote: AUC must be multiplied by 2 for a 12-hour dosing interval to calculate the true AUC 24

equations.name: Elimination rate constant from two levels
equations.text: Ke = ln(C1/C2)/(t1 - t2), as printed in the source
equations.caveat: Source prints the denominator as 't 1 - t 2' without brackets; the engine uses the elapsed time between the two draws (later minus earlier) so ke is positive. The worksheet source writes the same quantity as [Ln(C2) - Ln(C1)]/(T2 - T1), which is negative ke.
equations.quote: Calculate observed K e from 2 levels | K e = ln (C 1 /C 2 )/t 1 − t 2

equations.name: True peak (Cmax), back-extrapolated from the first level
equations.caveat: Source writes the exponent time as 'tin' (infusion time). The worksheet source uses Tp; the engine should use the time from end of infusion to the first draw. Reviewer to confirm.

equations.name: True trough (Cmin), extrapolated to the end of the dosing interval
equations.text: Cmin = Cmax x e^(-ke x (tau - tin))

equations.name: AUC during infusion (linear trapezoid)
equations.caveat: Source prints 'AUC inf = t in (Cmax + Cmin/2)'; the trapezoid is tin times the mean of Cmin and Cmax. The worksheet source writes '[Ce + Ct(zero if loading dose))/2) x infusion duration', which supports the bracketed reading. For a first (loading) dose the starting concentration is zero.
equations.quote: Calculate AUC during infusion using linear trapezoidal rule | AUC inf = t in (Cmax + Cmin/2)

equations.name: AUC during infusion (worksheet form, zero start concentration after a loading dose)
equations.text: Area during infusion = [Ce + Ct (zero if loading dose)]/2 x infusion duration
equations.quote: Area during infusion = [Ce + Ct(zero if loading dose))/2) x infusion duration

equations.name: AUC during elimination (log-down, mono-exponential integral)
equations.caveat: Source labels this row 'linear trapezoidal rule', but (Cmax - Cmin)/Ke is the exact integral of the mono-exponential decline (the log-down part of a linear-up log-down calculation). The worksheet source instead uses a linear trapezoid, (Ce + Ct)/2 x time, for the post-infusion area; that overestimates AUC. Reviewer to choose.
equations.quote: Calculate AUC during elimination using linear trapezoidal rule | AUC elim = (Cmax − Cmin)/K e

equations.name: Daily AUC from one dosing interval
equations.caveat: Source prints 'AUC inf + AUC elim (24/tau)' without brackets; the guideline (sampling note) scales the whole interval AUC by doses per day.
equations.quote: Calculate AUC 24 | AUC 24 = AUC inf + AUC elim (24/tau)

notes.text: Neonatal SCr is unreliable in the first week of life because of transplacental maternal creatinine.
notes.quote: SCr- based dosing (except for the first week of life, when transplacental maternal cre- atinine in the neonatal circulation ren- ders neonatal SCr values inaccurate in estimating renal function)

notes.text: The equation method gives only a snapshot and is not adaptive; it is wrong if renal function changes during sampling. Bayesian estimation is preferred.
notes.quote: The major limitation of this approach is that it is not adaptive like the Bayesian approach, as it can only provide a snapshot of the AUC for the sampling period.

hartford.label: Hartford once-daily aminoglycoside program (adults, 2,184 patients). Not validated in neonates.

dose_interval.quote: We initiated an ODA program at our institution that utilizes a fixed 7-mg/kg intravenous dose with a drug administration interval based on estimated creatinine clearance: > or = 60 ml/min every 24 h (q24h), 59 to 40 ml/min q36h, and 39 to 20 ml/min q48h. Subsequent interval adjustments are made by using a single concentration in serum and a nomogram designed for monitoring of ODA therapy.

level_window.quote: If once daily dosing was used, obtaining a mid-interval gentamicin concentration 6–14 hours post initial dose administration, followed by Hartford nomogram assessment was considered appropriate.

hartford.nomogram_lines_missing: The nomogram graph (concentration versus hours boundary lines for q24h, q36h, q48h) is a figure in the scanned 1995 article and could not be retrieved as text. Not stored.

nice.label: Measure trough immediately before the second dose
nice.quote: If giving a second dose of gentamicin, measure the trough blood gentamicin concentration immediately before giving the second dose. Take the trough concentrations into account before giving the third dose of gentamicin.

nice.label: Trough target
nice.quote: Adjust the gentamicin dose interval, aiming to achieve trough concentrations of less than 2 mg/litre. If the course of gentamicin lasts for more than 3 doses, aim for a trough concentration of less than 1 mg/litre.

nice.label: Consider peak levels in selected babies (for example macrosomia, birthweight more than 4.5 kg)
Peak drawn 1 hour after starting gentamicin
nice.quote: When measuring peak blood gentamicin concentrations, take the measurement 1 hour after starting gentamicin.

nice.label: Gram-negative or staphylococcal infection: consider a higher dose if peak is below 8 mg/litre
nice.quote: If a baby has a Gram-negative or staphylococcal infection, consider increasing the dose of gentamicin if the peak concentration is less than 8 mg/litre.

nice.label: Do not withhold a dose while waiting for a trough unless renal impairment
nice.quote: Do not withhold a dose of gentamicin because of delays in getting a trough concentration measurement, unless there is evidence of impaired renal function

fda.label: Pediatric label: avoid prolonged peaks above 12 mcg/mL and troughs above 2 mcg/mL
fda.quote: When monitoring peak concentrations after intramuscular or intravenous administration, dosage should be adjusted so that prolonged levels above 12 mcg/mL are avoided. When monitoring trough concentrations (just prior to the next dose), dosage should be adjusted so that levels above 2 mcg/mL are avoided.

fda.label: Expected peak after IM injection
fda.quote: For example, the peak concentration (at 30 to 60 minutes after intramuscular injection) is expected to be in the range of 3 to 5 mcg/mL.

fda.label: Serum half-life in premature infants by weight
fda.quote: In premature infants weighing less than 1500 grams, the half-life is 11 ½ hours; in those weighing 1500 to 2000 grams, the half-life is eight hours; in those weighing over 2000 grams, the half-life is approximately five hours.
